cap: Testosterone is low in both forms of hypogonadism, so LH decides the site. A failing testis cannot answer, so LH and FSH rise (primary, hypergonadotropic). A failing hypothalamus or pituitary stays silent, so LH and FSH are low or inappropriately normal (secondary, hypogonadotropic). Inhibin B from Sertoli cells restrains FSH selectively. Exogenous androgens suppress LH and FSH and shrink the testes, whereas obstructive azoospermia leaves hormones and testis size normal.
teach: Order LH before prescribing testosterone. Primary failure is untreatable at the testis, and fertility needs sperm retrieval. Secondary failure is often treatable: gonadotropins (hCG with FSH) restart spermatogenesis, and clomiphene raises endogenous LH and FSH. Obesity lowers SHBG and raises aromatization, so total testosterone can look low or normal while LH stays inappropriately normal. Injected androgens also raise the hematocrit, so hematocrit and PSA are monitored during testosterone therapy.
